questions.q: In a Mahakumbh, a drone camera is moving along $3y=x^3-3$. When y-coordinate changes 9 times as fast as x-coordinate, it captures good quality pictures. Then one of the precise positions of the drone at that instant is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^2=9\Rightarrow x=\pm3$. At $x=3$: $3y=27-3=24\Rightarrow y=8$, giving the point $(3,8)$.

questions.q: A Youtube short video is getting viral according to $f(t)=-2t^3+3t^2+5$. At what time does the video get maximum number of shares? (t is in hours)
questions.explanation: $f'(t)=-6t^2+6t=6t(1-t)=0\Rightarrow t=0,1$. $f''(t)=-12t+6$; at $t=1$, $f''=-6<0$, so maximum occurs at $t=1$.

questions.q: The minimum value of 1 - sin x is
questions.explanation: sin x has maximum value 1, so 1 - sin x has minimum value 0.

questions.q: The function f(x) = tan x - x
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=\sec^2x-1=\tan^2x\geq0$ for all x, so f is always (non-decreasing) increasing.

questions.q: For the function $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+12x-3$; $x=2$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=3x^2-12x+12$ so $f'(2)=0$; $f''(x)=6x-12$ so $f''(2)=0$; $f'''(2)=6\neq0$, hence $x=2$ is a point of inflexion.

questions.q: If $f(x)=xe^{x(1-x)}$ then $f(x)$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=e^{x-x^2}(1+x-2x^2)$. Since $e^{x-x^2}>0$, the sign is that of $1+x-2x^2=-(2x+1)(x-1)$, which is $\ge0$ for $x\in[-1/2,1]$; hence $f$ is increasing there.

questions.q: The function $x^x; x>0$ is strictly increasing at
questions.explanation: For $f(x)=x^x$, $f'(x)=x^x(1+\log x)$, which is positive when $1+\log x>0$, i.e. $x>\dfrac1e$.

questions.q: The maximum volume of the right circular cone with slant height 6 units is
questions.explanation: With $l^2=r^2+h^2=36$, $V=\dfrac{\pi}{3}(36-h^2)h$. Maximising gives $h^2=12,r^2=24$, so $V_{max}=16\sqrt3\pi$ cubic units.

questions.q: A circular plate of radius 5 cm is heated. Due to expansion, its radius increases at the rate of 0.05 cm/sec. The rate at which its area is increasing when the radius is 5.2 cm is
questions.explanation: $A=\pi r^2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 2\pi(5.2)(0.05) = 0.52\pi$ cm$^2$/sec.

questions.q: The distance 's' in meters travelled by a particle in 't' seconds is given by $s = \dfrac{2t^3}{3} - 18t + \dfrac{5}{3}$. The acceleration when the particle comes to rest is
questions.explanation: $v = 2t^2-18 = 0 \Rightarrow t=3$ (rest). $a = 4t = 12$ m/sec$^2$.

questions.q: A particle moves along the curve $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$. When the rate of change of abscissa is 4 times that of its ordinate, then the quadrant in which the particle lies is
questions.explanation: Differentiating and substituting $dx/dt = 4\,dy/dt$ gives $x+y=0$, i.e. $y=-x$; on the ellipse this occurs in quadrants II and IV.

questions.q: An enemy fighter jet is flying along the curve given by $y = x^2 + 2$. A soldier is placed at $(3, 2)$ wants to shoot down the jet when it is nearest to him. Then the nearest distance is
questions.explanation: Minimizing $D^2=(x-3)^2+x^4$ gives $2x^3+x-3=0$ with root $x=1$, point $(1,3)$; distance $=\sqrt{(1-3)^2+(3-2)^2}=\sqrt5$.

questions.q: The function f(x) = log(1 + x) - $\dfrac{2x}{2+x}$ is increasing on
questions.explanation: $f'(x) = \frac{1}{1+x} - \frac{4}{(2+x)^2} = \frac{x^2}{(1+x)(2+x)^2} \ge 0$ whenever $x>-1$, so f is increasing on $(-1,\infty)$.

questions.q: The co-ordinates of the point on the $\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y}=6$ at which the tangent is equally inclined to the axes is
questions.explanation: Differentiating, y'=-\sqrt{y}/\sqrt{x}. Equally inclined means slope magnitude 1, so x=y; then $2\sqrt{x}=6\Rightarrow x=y=9$.

questions.q: The function f(x) = 4 sin$^3$x - 6 sin$^2$x + 12 sin x + 100 is strictly
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=12\cos x(\sin^2x-\sin x+1)$; the quadratic factor is always positive, so the sign of f'(x) equals the sign of $\cos x$, which is negative on $(\pi/2,\pi)$, making f strictly decreasing there.

questions.q: A particle starts from rest and its angular displacement (in radians) is given by $\theta=\dfrac{t^2}{20}+\dfrac{t}{5}$. If the angular velocity at the end of t = 4 is k, then the value of 5k is
questions.explanation: $\omega=d\theta/dt=t/10+1/5$; at t=4, $\omega$=0.6=k, so 5k=3.

questions.q: If the parabola y = $\alpha$x$^2$ $-$ 6x + $\beta$ passes through the point (0, 2) and has its tangent at x = 3/2 parallel to x axis, then
questions.explanation: Passing through (0,2) gives $\beta$=2; the tangent slope 2$\alpha$x$-$6=0 at x=3/2 gives $\alpha$=2.

questions.q: The function f(x) = x$^2$ $-$ 2x is strictly decreasing in the interval
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 2x $-$ 2 < 0 gives x < 1, so f is strictly decreasing on ($-\infty$, 1).

questions.q: The maximum slope of the curve y = $-$x$^3$ + 3x$^2$ + 2x $-$ 27 is
questions.explanation: Slope y' = $-3x^2+6x+2$; maximizing gives x=1, so maximum slope = $-3+6+2=5$.

questions.q: If the curves $2x=y^2$ and $2xy=K$ intersect perpendicularly, then the value of $K^2$ is
questions.explanation: Slopes are $1/y$ and $-y/x$; perpendicularity gives $x=1$, then $y=\sqrt2$ from $2x=y^2$, so $K=2xy=2\sqrt2$ and $K^2=8$.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\dfrac{\log_e x}{x}$, if $x>0$ is
questions.explanation: Setting derivative $(1-\log x)/x^2=0$ gives $x=e$, and the maximum value is $1/e$.

questions.q: If the side of a cube is increased by 5%, then the surface area of a cube is increased by
questions.explanation: Using differentials, $dS/S\approx 2(da/a)=2(5\%)=10\%$ (question was given a grace mark by KEA, as the exact increase is $10.25\%$).

questions.q: The interval in which the function $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+9x+10$ is increasing in
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=3(x-1)(x-3)\ge0$ for $x\le1$ or $x\ge3$, so $f$ is increasing on $(-\infty,1]\cup[3,\infty)$.

questions.q: The sides of an equilateral triangle are increasing at the rate of 4 cm/sec. The rate at which its area is increasing, when the side is 14 cm
questions.explanation: For side $s$, $A=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}s\dfrac{ds}{dt}$. With $s=14,\ ds/dt=4$ this gives $28\sqrt3$ cm$^2$/sec, which matches none of the printed options exactly (it equals $14\sqrt3$ only if $s=7$); KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The value of $\sqrt{24.99}$ is
questions.explanation: Using differentials, $\sqrt{25-0.01}\approx 5-\dfrac{0.01}{2\times5}=4.999$.

questions.q: Approximate change in the volume V of a cube of side x metres caused by increasing the side by 3% is
The maximum value of $\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^x$ is
questions.explanation: Taking logs and differentiating, the maximum occurs at $x=1/e$, giving value $e^{1/e}$.

questions.q: $f(x)=x^x$ has stationary point at
questions.explanation: $\ln f=x\ln x$; $f'/f=\ln x+1=0\Rightarrow x=1/e$.

questions.q: The maximum area of a rectangle inscribed in the circle $(x+1)^2+(y-3)^2=64$ is
questions.explanation: For a circle of radius r, the maximum inscribed rectangle (a square) has area $2r^2$; here $r^2=64$, so area $=128$ sq. units.

questions.q: The point on the curve $y^2=x$ where the tangent makes an angle of $\pi/4$ with X-axis is
questions.explanation: $2y\,dy/dx=1\Rightarrow dy/dx=\dfrac{1}{2y}=\tan(\pi/4)=1\Rightarrow y=\dfrac12,\ x=y^2=\dfrac14$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=x^2+2x-5$ is strictly increasing in the interval
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=2x+2>0$ when $x>-1$, so f is strictly increasing on $(-1,\infty)$.

questions.q: The rate of change of volume of a sphere with respect to its surface area when the radius is 4 cm is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dV}{dS}=\dfrac{dV/dr}{dS/dr}=\dfrac{4\pi r^2}{8\pi r}=\dfrac r2=2\ cm^3/cm^2$ at $r=4$.

questions.q: The slope of the tangent to the curve $x = t^2 + 3t - 8,\ y = 2t^2 - 2t - 5$ at the point (2, -1) is
questions.explanation: The point (2,-1) corresponds to $t=2$; then $dx/dt=2t+3=7$, $dy/dt=4t-2=6$, so slope $=dy/dx=6/7$.

questions.q: The two curves $x^3 - 3xy^2 + 2 = 0$ and $3x^2y - y^3 = 2$
options: Cut each other at right angle
questions.explanation: Differentiating both curves gives slopes $m_1=\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{2xy}$ and $m_2=\dfrac{-2xy}{x^2-y^2}$; since $m_1m_2=-1$ always, the curves are orthogonal (cut at right angle).

questions.q: The equation of the normal to the curve $y(1+x^2) = 2 - x$ where the tangent crosses x-axis is
questions.explanation: Where the curve meets the x-axis, $y=0 \Rightarrow x=2$; differentiating gives slope $-1/5$ at (2,0), so the normal slope is 5, giving $y=5(x-2)$, i.e. $5x-y-10=0$.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^x$ is
questions.explanation: Let $y=x^{-x}$; taking logs and differentiating, the maximum occurs at $x=1/e$, giving $y=e^{1/e}$.

questions.q: The rate of change of area of a circle with respect to its radius at r = 2 cms is
questions.explanation: $A=\pi r^2 \Rightarrow dA/dr=2\pi r$; at $r=2$, $dA/dr=4\pi$.

questions.q: Slope of Normal to the curve $y = x^2 - \dfrac{1}{x^2}$ at $(-1, 0)$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x+\dfrac{2}{x^3}$; at $x=-1$ this is $-4$, so slope of normal $=-1/(-4)=1/4$.

questions.q: A balloon which always remains spherical is being inflated by pumping in 10 cubic centimeters of gas per second. Find the rate at which the radius of the balloon is increasing when the radius is 15 cms.
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}=10\Rightarrow \dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{10}{4\pi(225)}=\dfrac{1}{90\pi}$.

questions.q: The two curves $x^3-3xy^2+2=0$ and $3x^2y-y^3=2$
questions.explanation: These are the real and imaginary parts of $z^3=\text{const}$-type families, which are known to be mutually orthogonal, so the curves cut at right angles.

questions.q:
If f(x) = $x^3$ and g(x) = $x^3-4x$ in $-2\le x\le2$, then consider the statements:
(a) f(x) and g(x) satisfy mean value theorem.
(b) f(x) and g(x) both satisfy Rolle's theorem.
(c) Only g(x) satisfies Rolle's theorem.
Of these statements
questions.explanation: Both functions are continuous and differentiable, so MVT holds (a). g(-2)=g(2)=0 so g satisfies Rolle's theorem, but f(-2)$\neq$f(2) so f does not; hence only (a) and (c) are correct.

questions.q: The tangent to the curve y = $x^3+1$ at (1, 2) makes an angle $\theta$ with y axis, then the value of tan $\theta$ is
questions.note: Standard convention (acute angle with the y-axis) gives tan theta = 1/3 (option A); KEA's key credits -1/3 (option D), which corresponds to the supplementary angle on the other side of the tangent line.
questions.explanation: $dy/dx=3x^2=3$ at x=1, the slope with the x-axis (key column confirmed as B-3). Taking the acute angle between the tangent and the y-axis gives $\tan\theta=1/3$, but KEA's key credits $-1/3$.

questions.q: The local minimum value of the function f given by f(x) = $3+|x|$, $x\in R$ is
questions.explanation: f(x)=3+|x| has its minimum at x=0 where f(0)=3; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: A stone is dropped into a quiet lake and waves move in circles at the speed of 5 cm/sec. At that instant, when the radius of circular wave is 8 cm, how fast is the enclosed area increasing?
questions.explanation: A=$\pi r^2$, so $dA/dt = 2\pi r\,dr/dt = 2\pi(8)(5)=80\pi$ cm$^2$/s.

questions.q: A gardener is digging a plot of land. As he gets tired, he works more slowly. After 't' minutes he is digging at a rate of $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt t}$ square metres per minute. How long will it take him to dig an area of 40 square metres?
questions.explanation: Area dug $=\int_0^t\frac{2}{\sqrt t}\,dt = 4\sqrt t$. Setting $4\sqrt t=40$ gives $\sqrt t=10$, so $t=100$ minutes.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{3}{x}$ decreases in the interval
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=\dfrac13-\dfrac{3}{x^2}<0\Rightarrow x^2<9\Rightarrow -3<x<3$.

questions.q: If $\sin^{-1}a$ is the acute angle between the curves $x^2+y^2=4x$ and $x^2+y^2=8$ at $(2,2)$, then $a=$
questions.explanation: The tangent slopes at $(2,2)$ are 0 and $-1$, so $\tan\theta=1\Rightarrow\theta=45°$, giving $a=\sin45°=1/\sqrt2$.

questions.q: The maximum area of a rectangle that can be inscribed in a circle of radius 2 units is
questions.explanation: The maximum-area rectangle is a square with diagonal 4, giving side $2\sqrt2$ and area 8.

questions.q: If the length of the sub-tangent at any point to the curve $xy^n=a$ is proportional to the abscissa, then 'n' is
questions.explanation: The subtangent is $y/y'=-nx$, which is proportional to the abscissa x for any value of n.

questions.q: Length of the subtangent at $(x_1, y_1)$ on $x^n y^m = a^{m+n}$, $m, n > 0$, is
questions.explanation: Taking logs and differentiating, $y'=-\dfrac{ny}{mx}$. Subtangent $=y/y'=-\dfrac{mx}{n}$, whose magnitude is $\dfrac{m}{n}|x_1|$.

questions.q: If a ball is thrown vertically upwards and the height 's' reached in time 't' is given by $s = 22t - 11t^2$, then the total distance travelled by the ball is
questions.explanation: $v=22-22t=0$ at $t=1$, giving maximum height $s=11$. Since the ball returns to the start ($s=0$ at $t=0,2$), total distance $=2\times11=22$ units.

questions.q: The sum of two positive numbers is given. If the sum of their cubes is minimum, then
questions.explanation: With $x+y=k$ fixed, minimising $x^3+(k-x)^3$ gives $x=y=k/2$, so the numbers are equal.

questions.q: The perimeter of a sector is a constant. If its area is to be maximum, then the sectorial angle is
questions.explanation: With perimeter $k=2r+r\theta$ fixed, area $A=\tfrac12 r(k-2r)$; maximising over $r$ gives $r=k/4$ and then $\theta=2$ radians.

questions.q: The tangent to the curve $xy = 25$ at any point on it cuts the coordinate axes at A and B, then the area of the triangle OAB is
questions.explanation: For $xy=c^2$, the tangent at $(x_1,y_1)$ meets the axes at $(2x_1,0)$ and $(0,2y_1)$, so area $=\tfrac12(2x_1)(2y_1)=2x_1y_1=2(25)=50$.

questions.q: The length of the sub-tangent, ordinate and the sub-normal are in
questions.explanation: Subtangent $=y/y'$ and subnormal $=yy'$; their product is $y^2$, the square of the ordinate, so the three are in G.P.

questions.q: The maximum value of $xe^{-x}$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=e^{-x}(1-x)=0$ at $x=1$, giving the maximum value $f(1)=1/e$.

questions.q: Area of a triangle formed by tangent and normal to the curve $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ at $P\left(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt2},\dfrac{b}{\sqrt2}\right)$ with the $X$-axis is ........
questions.explanation: The tangent meets the $X$-axis at $(a\sqrt2,0)$ and the normal meets it at $\left(\dfrac{a^2-b^2}{a\sqrt2},0\right)$; with the height $b/\sqrt2$ from $P$, the triangle's area works out to $\dfrac{b(a^2+b^2)}{4a}$.

questions.q: The angle between $y^2=4x$ and $x^2+y^2=12$ at a point of their intersection is ............
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $(2,2\sqrt2)$, where the slopes are $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$; the angle between them is $\tan^{-1}(2\sqrt2)$.

questions.q: A sphere increases its volume at the rate of $\pi$ cc/s. The rate at which its surface area increases when the radius is 1 cm is ............
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\pi$ gives $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{4r^2}$. Then $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=8\pi r\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{2\pi}{r}$, which at $r=1$ is $2\pi$ sq.cm/s.

questions.q: $P$ is the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the curve $y=\log_e x$. The length of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the normal at $P$ is
questions.explanation: The tangent from the origin touches at $P=(e,1)$ (since the tangent line $y-\ln x_0=(x-x_0)/x_0$ passes through the origin only when $x_0=e$); the normal there is $ex+y-(e^2+1)=0$, whose distance from the origin is $\sqrt{e^2+1}$.

questions.q: For the curve $4x^5=5y^4$, the ratio of the cube of the subtangent at a point on the curve to the square of the subnormal at the same point is
questions.explanation: With $y'=x^4/y^3$, the subtangent is $y^4/x^4$ and the subnormal is $x^4/y^2$; using $y^4=(4/5)x^5$, the ratio (subtangent)$^3$/(subnormal)$^2$ simplifies to $(4/5)^4$.

questions.q: The set of real values of $x$ for which $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{\log x}$ is increasing, is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=\dfrac{\log x-1}{(\log x)^2}\ge0$ requires $\log x\ge1$, i.e. $x\ge e$.

questions.q: A wire of length 20 cm is bent in the form of a sector of a circle. The maximum area that can be enclosed by the wire is
questions.explanation: With perimeter $2r+r\theta=20$, area $A=10r-r^2$; maximizing gives $r=5$ and $A=25$ sq. cm.

questions.q: The tangent to a given curve $y = f(x)$ is perpendicular to the x-axis if
questions.explanation: A tangent perpendicular to the x-axis is a vertical line, i.e. its slope is infinite; equivalently $\dfrac{dx}{dy}=0$.

questions.q: The minimum value of $27^{\cos2x}\,81^{\sin2x}$ is
questions.explanation: The expression equals $3^{3\cos2x+4\sin2x}$; since $3\cos2x+4\sin2x$ ranges over $[-5,5]$, the minimum value is $3^{-5}=1/243$.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upwards from the top of a tower 64 metres high according to the law $s = 48t - 16t^2$. The greatest height attained by the stone above the ground is
questions.explanation: $s$ is maximum when $ds/dt=48-32t=0 \Rightarrow t=1.5$, giving $s_{max}=48(1.5)-16(1.5)^2=36$; total height above ground $=64+36=100$ metres.

questions.q: The length of the subtangent at 't' on the curve $x = a(t + \sin t)$, $y = a(1 - \cos t)$ is
questions.explanation: Subtangent $= y\dfrac{dx}{dy} = a(1-\cos t)\cdot\dfrac{1+\cos t}{\sin t} = a\dfrac{\sin^2 t}{\sin t} = a\sin t$.
